To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The phase diagram for a given system is a map of the thermodynamic stability of the phases involved, and so provides the basis for predicting the mutual reactivity of the phases.

(a) The chemical reactivity of a thin film at a given temperature is determined by its Gibbs free energy, and that (b) the Gibbs free energies of the phases present at a given temperature can be calculated using the CALPHAD method.

(i) The thermodynamics of thin-film reactions may be understood in terms of phase diagrams, (ii) Phase diagram data for multicomponent systems can be calculated from known data for binary systems, (iii) The stability of a phase diagram can be determined from the sign of the free energy difference between the phases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction, and control, of chemical reactions in microelectronic devices.
the application of thermodynamics to microelectronics.
the application of phase diagram theory to microelectronic device fabrication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase diagram approach is a valuable aid in the prediction and understanding of metallization reactions, and that the principles involved are of general applicability.
the use of phase diagrams, or the calculation of new ones, is a very powerful tool in the design and optimization of semiconductor metallization systems.

the phase diagram is a useful tool to predict and understand the stability of the phases at the metallization-semiconductor interface, and that the application of this tool is not restricted to the systems described in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of phase diagram theory to thin-film reactions has proved to be a powerful predictive tool.
, by application of phase diagram methods, it is possible to predict the chemical reactivity at interfaces in microelectronic devices.
the principles of phase stability are applicable in the microelectronic field, and that they can provide a basis for the rational design of new materials and processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phase diagrams are a valuable and under-utilized resource for predicting and understanding the chemical reactivity of materials at interfaces.

the phase diagram approach is a powerful and general tool for the analysis and understanding of thin-film reactions, and that the phase stability or reactivity of a given interface can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy.
the application of phase diagram concepts to thin-film reactions is not only possible but also useful in the design of microelectronic structures.
